title: Minimising the harmonic sum of cycle lengths
summary: A central theme in extremal graph theory is to understand the relationship between the density of a graph and the richness of its cycle length spectrum, which is the set of distinct cycle lengths occurring in the graph. In 1966, Erdős and Hajnal suggested studying $s(G):=\sum_{\ell\in{C}(G)}1/\ell$ as a measure of the richness of the cycle length spectrum ${C}(G)$ of a graph $G$. Through a series of increasingly strong conjectures, Erdős suggested that the complete bipartite graphs minimise $s(G)$ among all graphs $G$ with the same average degree.
